Question: Are mutual exclusivity and independence the same thing?

Choices.A: No. Mutually exclusive means the events cannot occur simultaneously; independent means whether one occurs does not affect whether the other occurs
Choices.B: Yes, the two terms mean exactly the same thing
Choices.C: Yes, mutually exclusive events must be independent
Choices.D: No, independent means the two events have equal probabilities

Solution: When both probabilities are positive, mutually exclusive events cannot be independent, because once one occurs, the conditional probability of the other becomes \(0\).
